It used to blow a whistle all the people to go to the chief's place and.

All the people or all the animals they go and listen the chief is saying what and the chief was staying far.

I heard like the chief said like that.

In another village, there were animals.
One of these animals was Rabbit.
And the other animals were doing work.
When it got to the time of planting food.
All the animals were going to plant on their farms.
But Rabbit was more wise than the other animals.
While people were planting, the rabbit was asleep.
So, people were wondering, "This one is always asleep while others are planting."
"We do not see hunger hurting him, and we do not see him losing weight."
"And again, we do not know where he is getting the things that he is eating."
When it got to the time of harvesting, it used to blow a whistle and the people would go to the chief's place.
And it was a law that when a whistle is blown, all the animals would go and listen to what the chief was saying.
And the chief lived far away.
So, while the people had gone to the chief's place to hear what he was saying, Rabbit was coming back and stealing things quickly from people.
It would go and hide them in the house.
So, when the people had arrived at the chief's place, the chief would tell them, "I did not send the rabbit."
"Go and ask him what he was referring to."
When they returned and asked him, he would say, "Oo, I was refering to the following month or the following week."
"I thought I heard the chief say that."
So, it went like this several times and people got tired.
And then they got to a point where they said, "Now, when he blows again, we shall not go.
"We will go back and we will trap him here."
So truly, the time came again that the rabbit wanted to steal from people.
It blew the whistle for the people to go.
Some people lied that they had gone and others remained in the house in the farms to see what is happening.
So, when the rabbit thought that all of the people had gone, it started to enter the house.
Then, when people came out, they blew the whistle again and they caught him.
They told him, "It's you who usually steals from us?
"Now that we have found you, let's go to the chief's place where you said."
So, they took him to the chief's place at the court.
They sued the rabbit and they sentenced him to go work on all the people's farms.
Since then, Rabbit learned to work hard like the other animals.
As for names, I am Billy Jivetti and I want to talk about Tiriki circumcision rites.
In the village or community of the Tiriki, circumcision is a very important thing because circumcision makes one graduate from childhood to adulthood, from boyhood to manhood.
So this very thing, in Tiriki traditions, is very respected.
Since the old days, in the years that were of our forefathers, up to today, we still practice these things.
Circumcision is held in Tirikiland every five years.
Like me I went through circumcision in 1985, and my ageset is called Ndalo II.
Before I underwent circumcision, my father sat me down and told me I am now the right age of a boy.
They want to go teach me the traditions of our elders.
I’m about to become a man.
The things that i used to do as a young boy and the games i used to play with small girls at home now I need to stop.
because I’m about to become a respected man.
Now after you become a man, they separate you in the things you do.
You are not expected to be a cry-baby or a person who is easily provoked or if something happens you get scared scared.
Circumcision makes you a man who is hardened not afraid of taking risks.
I underwent circumcision when I was about eight years old.
And this is about the age when most young boys begin undergoing circumcision.
When you are about to undergo circumcision, they take you to sleep with the most senior elder.
That night they teach you the traditions and tell you you all are going to become this ageset.
And you all will grow up of people of the same ageset.
Among these people when you age, if one of you dies, they will call upon you (all) to stand up, go, and bury him.
And that’s how we have lived all these years.
Every man or young man who has undergone circumcision among the Tiriki belongs to a certain ageset.
And the elders in the circumcision period are very respected because these are the people carrying all the traditions of this Tiriki community.
And the most surprising things includes the things we are taught during circumcision.
After being circumcised, they tell you that women are not supposed to know these things.
So they made this thing to be a secret for the women because they say if women know this secret they will dispise us as men.
And the things they teach us are many.
It’s to look after your wife if you are married (if you have your own house) or if you are a leader.
They teach you all those things.
We are circumcised in the forest very early in the morning after leaving where you slept.
And they use a very sharp knife.
When you feel pain you are not supposed to cry or they will see that you were not yet ready to become a man.
But if you just remain quiet despite feeling the pain, then people will be very happy; they’ll say yes this one is a real man.
When you leave that place, then we will go stay in the bush for a whole month.
Women don’t come there at all.
It’s just circumcised youth who come out.
And other old men come to teach us our culture as Tirikis.
This circumcision practice has two factions.
The people who began this circumcision practice still put on animal skins, skins of monkeys, of any other (animals) to cover themselves (with).
But these people, as the years progressed, people became educated
They realized (saw) they need to move on from the practices they are doing.
These skin-wearers perceive themselves to be the real Tirikis or the original Tiriki founders of circumcision.
These people do things like abuses.

But when the church came and said, "we want to transform circumcision to be a good thing and bring in Christianity and education', so the educated people who take (their children) to the bush call themselves “Vasoomi.”
The “vasoomi” are a group of people you would call “reformists” in English.
People who have reformed from the original Tiriki circumcision rites [code-switching] those do things in sync with “modern society”.
And they have given up those other things.
So this is the practice that I like.
Even while I am here [in the US], I keep looking to see what is happening, knowing that I am a Tiriki and what makes me a Tiriki like this (is that) I was circumcized as a Tiriki.
And even if I stand now and I want to be a leader among the Tiriki they will accept me because I am their son, I went through the circumcision rites and they took care of me.

People who were still young or men in the villages are the ones who used to go herd in those forests because the forests in which they used to herd were far away.
And wild animals were in those forests (too).

So one day, young boys left the village to go look after the cows in the forest.

This is a story about Elephant and Rabbit.
Elephant and Rabbit were staying in a certain community.
And they were very good friends.
They liked each other and did things together.
They would go together looking for things for their children to eat.
Elephant had a calf while Rabbit had a baby (rabbit).
Because the parents were friends, the children, the calf and baby rabbit, also became friends.
And did things together happily, because they would see that their parents liked each other a lot.
Because Rabbit had a small body.
Other animals such as foxes (wolves?) had a habit of hunting and eating small animals such as Rabbit.
While Elephant was a big animal, that other animals feared.
Because it has tusks and huge legs.
So Rabbit would hide under (“in”) Elephant.
So foxes and other animals would not bully her (Rabbit).
Or when she would cause trouble out there, she would go hide herself by Elephant.
Elephant would chase away the other animals.
So they would do a lot of things together and their friendship grew.
Others were just wondering these people like each other so much, why is that.
Because they saw the friendship has really progressed without them disagreeing.
Because Rabbit had made some enemies.
And those enemies could not get to Rabbit easily.
Because Elephant was fierce and would protect Rabbit.
So one day they left to do their work together.
And they disagreed; they fought each other there.
They would disagree IDEO; they would fight all the time.
But as friends they would come back and agree.
They would forgive each other and then they would continue being friends.
But on this day Elephant was so furious.
The way rabbit had done so Elephant just grabbed Rabbit.
And threw (her) down and stepped on (her).
Because she is a small animal Rabbit just died like that.
So Elephant reached somewhere and it dawned on him,
So who will I walk with?
Who will be telling me what is happening here?
Ohh Elephant was so sad he said he had made a big mistake.
He was not supposed to kill.
It should just have been as they usually are when they disagree.
So the child of Rabbit heard they had killed (his) mother.
And wondered now who will be helping him (and) feeding him,
it does not have the strength to fight with the elephant calf.
Instead it looked for poison to put in the food of the Elephant calf.
The elephant calf ate that very food and then it died.
So when Elephant came, he searched (and wondered).
with the baby rabbit, where have they gone?”

The stomach is swollen it looks as if someone fed (it) poison.

He ran and went off for good.
So he would other animals who would stop and ask.
